examples.question_text:
An account starts with $\$658$ and earns $3.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
(a) Show the balance at the end of each of the first $3$ years, to the nearest cent.
(b) Explain why adding $\$23.03$ each year would not give compound interest.
examples.solution_text:
Multiplier $=1.035$.
Year $1$: $\$658\times1.035=\$681.03$.
Year $2$: $\$681.03\times1.035=\$704.86605$, so the displayed balance is $\$704.87$.
Keep the unrounded value for year $3$:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\$704.86605\times1.035\\&=\$729.53636175\\&\approx\$729.54\end{aligned}$
(b) $\$23.03$ is the first year’s interest on $\$658$. Each new year uses the larger current balance, so its interest is larger.

examples.question_text:
A fund holds $\$843.25$ at the end of year $2$. It earns $4.2\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
(a) Find the balance at the end of year $3$.
(b) Find the interest earned in year $3$.
Give both answers to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Apply the multiplier once more:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\$843.25\times1.042\\&=\$878.6665\\&\approx\$878.67\end{aligned}$
(b) Year $3$ starts with $\$843.25$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Interest}&=\$843.25\times0.042\\&=\$35.4165\\&\approx\$35.42\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
An account starts with $\$724$ and earns $5.3\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
(a) Find the balance after $2$ years.
(b) Find the total interest earned in those $2$ years.
Give both answers to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
Year $1$: $\$724\times1.053=\$762.372$.
Year $2$: $\$762.372\times1.053=\$802.777716$.
(a) Balance $\approx\$802.78$.
(b) Total interest:
$\begin{aligned}I&=\$802.777716-\$724\\&\approx\$78.78\end{aligned}$
The balance includes the original deposit; the interest does not.

examples.question_text:
An account starts with $\$416$ and earns $7.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the interest earned in year $3$, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
Year $1$ ends with $\$416\times1.075=\$447.20$.
Year $2$ ends with $\$447.20\times1.075=\$480.74$.
Year $3$ interest:
$\begin{aligned}I_3&=\$480.74\times0.075\\&=\$36.0555\\&\approx\$36.06\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: After $2$ years at $4.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually, a fund holds $\$899.25$. Work backwards to find the deposit, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
Multiplier $=1.045$.
Undo each year by dividing:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\$899.25\div1.045\div1.045\\&\approx\$823.47\end{aligned}$
Keep the full calculator value after the first division.

examples.question_text:
A fund starts with $\$812.50$ and earns $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. The saver needs $\$936$.
At the end of which year does the balance first reach the target? Show why it has not reached the target in the preceding year.
examples.solution_text:
Multiplier $=1.05$.
Year $1$: $\$812.50\times1.05=\$853.125$.
Year $2$: $\$853.125\times1.05=\$895.78125$.
Year $3$:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\$895.78125\times1.05\\&=\$940.5703125\end{aligned}$
Year $2$ is below $\$936$; year $3$ is above it.
The balance first reaches the target at the end of year $3$.

examples.derivation: Successive multiplication by 1.035 gives 681.03, 704.86605 and 729.53636175; displayed balances are $681.03, $704.87 and $729.54. Fixed annual interest of $23.03 uses the original principal rather than the growing balance.
724 × 1.053 = 762.372; 762.372 × 1.053 = 802.777716. The balance rounds to $802.78; subtracting 724 gives interest of 78.777716, rounding to $78.78.
899.25 ÷ 1.045 ÷ 1.045 = 823.470158650214…, rounding to $823.47. Repeated division reverses the source's annual multiplier and is equivalent to its present-value rearrangement.
Successive multiplication by 1.05 gives 853.125, 895.78125 and 940.5703125. Year 2 is below $936 and year 3 exceeds it, so the first qualifying year is year 3.
